Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Key clinical findings: Acute, severely pruritic, sore, red and cracked skin on chest, hands, arms (esp. inside elbows); onset 4 days ago; significant disruption to sleep and daily function; no fever, bleeding, pus or discharge. Prior history of eczema, but more severe/widespread this episode. No new exposures identified; minimal benefit from OTC steroid cream and antihistamines.
- Working diagnosis: Atopic dermatitis (eczema) flare. Supported by clinical history, previous eczema, typical rash distribution, and symptomatology (DDx: High likelihood).
- DDx considerations: Contact dermatitis (Medium likelihood) due to possible unrecognized irritant, but patient denies new products/exposures. Allergic urticaria (Low likelihood)—no transient wheals. Skin infection (Low likelihood)—no crusting, lesions, or exudate.
- Management: Prescribed stronger topical steroid and emollients; recommended use 7–10 days. Advised trial of stronger antihistamine (Fexofenadine). Suggested diary for potential triggers and review if not improved.
- No evidence of systemic symptoms or infection at this stage.
- No conflicting information noted between transcript and DDx.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

- Atopic dermatitis (eczema) flare – High likelihood: History of eczema, current presentation matches clinical pattern but more severe/widespread; incomplete response to OTC treatment.
- Contact dermatitis (allergic or irritant) – Medium likelihood: Acute, intensely itchy rash in exposed areas; possible with environmental or product trigger, though not clearly identified by patient.
- Allergic urticaria – Low likelihood: Sudden pruritus, but rash lacks transient hives/wheals; does not match description.
